title: Use an alternate pronunciation cue
observableEvidence: Uses an alternate-pronunciation cue to distinguish spellings.
prompt: The pronouncer gives two accepted pronunciations for one invented word. In the first, BRAY-vul, the first vowel sounds like the name of the letter A. In the second, BRAV-ul, the first vowel sounds like the a in "cat". Which spelling can be read both ways under regular English spelling patterns? Enter one option exactly: bravel, brayvel, or braivel.
solutionRepresentation: bravel. A single vowel letter followed by one consonant and then another vowel can be read long or short in English (compare the real words "navel", said NAY-vul, and "gravel", said GRAV-ul), so bravel fits both pronunciations. The letter pairs ay and ai lock the vowel to the long sound, so brayvel and braivel fit only the first pronunciation.
solutionMethod: Check each spelling against both accepted pronunciations and keep the one that allows both.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Provisional SP-1 ruling C-1: contest mode keeps a legacy text validator whose only accepted answer is the exact option text listed in the prompt. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores trailing punctuation; any other wording is rejected.

hintSteps.prompt: Only the first vowel sound changes between the two pronunciations. The right spelling must allow both versions of that vowel.
hintSteps.question: Which part of each option spells the first vowel?

hintSteps.prompt: Some vowel spellings allow only one sound. A two-letter vowel spelling usually makes only the long sound.
hintSteps.question: Which options can be read only with the long vowel?

hintSteps.prompt: Example with a different vowel: if a word could be said both SEE-ten and SET-en, a spelling with a single e and a single t before the next vowel fits both, while a spelling with ee fits only the long one.
hintSteps.question: Using that idea, which option fits both pronunciations of this word?

accessibilityNotes: All information is presented in text. Sounds are described in words, not phonetic symbols. No visual formatting, audio or official list data is required.
accessibleAlternative: Two accepted pronunciations of one invented word: "bray-vul", where the first vowel sounds like the name of the letter A, and "brav-ul", where the first vowel sounds like the a in "cat". Both are stressed on the first part. Type the spelling, exactly as listed, that can be read both ways: bravel, brayvel, or braivel.
